tile_details.description: packed sand and dirt paths, no stone paving
short single-story mud-brick homes with flat roofs
old worn wooden planks, one small fishing boat always tied up
nets hung between poles to dry along fishermen's row
rocky cliffside overlooking the sea at northeast corner

night.note: very dark — no street torches, only doorway lanterns

contrast_vs_tyre.note: Everything in Kefr-Yamm should visually feel smaller, quieter, and older than Tyre. No purple. No marble. No crowds.

steps.description: Open inventory to see starting items
Buy any item from the shop
Sell an item from your inventory
Inspect your starting boat at the dock
Talk to Rib-Addi the blind sailor
Accept your first quest from Dagon
Sail for the first time — tutorial voyage to Sidon

visual.description: Three old wooden planks extending into the sea. One iron ring to tie boats. A crate used as a seat.

starting_ship.description: A small, battered fishing boat. It floats. Barely. Enough to reach Sidon or Tyre.

services.description: Opens the voyage map to choose a destination
Shows current ship stats and damage

services.note: Only basic repairs available here. Full repairs require Tyre shipwright.

visual.description: A low mud-brick building with an open front counter. Sacks of grain, bundles of rope, and clay pots stacked outside.
A stone well in the center of the village. Villagers gather here in the morning. The main place to hear local rumors.

outcome.description: Free rumors but only about nearby locations — Sidon and Tyre. Not useful for distant cities.
examples: A merchant in Sidon is paying double for dried fish this week
Tyre's harbor has been busy — lots of ships from Egypt, prices on grain are low
Someone saw a strange light on the cliffside last night

buildings.note: Contrast with Tyre's fountain rumor mechanic — this one is free but limited. Teaches player that better information costs more in bigger cities.

visual.description: The house you grew up in. Small, clean, smells of bread and fish oil. A sleeping mat, a small chest, and a window facing the sea.

services.description: Advances time to next morning. Restores player stamina if implemented.
Free item storage. Max 50 item slots. Safe from theft.

lines.speaker: mother_ashera
lines.text: You've been staring at those ships since you were a child. I always knew this day would come. Take what's in the chest. And come back.

lines.speaker: mother_ashera
lines.text: You went to Sidon and came back in one piece. I made fish stew. Tell me everything.

lines.speaker: mother_ashera
lines.text: The village is talking about you. Old Dagon says you've got a trader's eye. Your father had that too.

lore_notes.father: Player's father was also a merchant. Died at sea years ago. Mother Ashera never speaks of it directly unless prompted. This becomes important in later parts of the game.

lines.speaker: dagon
lines.text: Buy here cheap. Sell in Sidon or Tyre for more. That's all trading is. Don't let anyone tell you different.

lines.speaker: dagon
lines.text: Fish is worth more in Tyre — they've got rich merchants who want smoked fish and won't lower themselves to buy it from the harbor. Clay pots sell decent in Sidon.

lines.speaker: dagon
lines.text: Actually — I have a box that needs to get to a merchant in Sidon. I can't leave the shop. You're going anyway. I'll pay you 25 silver on top of whatever you make trading.

location.description: Sits at the end of the dock every day. Rain or shine.

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: You're going to sail. I can hear it. The way your feet stop at the dock edge — that's not a fisherman's pause. That's someone looking for something.

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: I went west once. Far west. Past where the maps end. I saw something. Green and enormous and impossible.

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: Nobody believed me. Doesn't matter. You will, someday. Go on. Sail. Come back and tell me what you find.

player_choices.text: Nod and walk to your boat

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: No. You wouldn't understand yet. See the world first. Then ask me again.

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: Past the Pillars. That's all I'll say. Past the Pillars, and keep sailing until you think you've made a terrible mistake. Then keep sailing.

lines.speaker: rib_addi
lines.text: You've been far. I can smell the different seas on you. Now. Sit down. I'll tell you what I saw.

rewards.description: He gives the player his old sailor rope bracelet as a keepsake

secret.description: Has seen the land beyond the Pillars of Hercules with his own eyes — before he went blind. His account contains one specific navigational detail not found anywhere else in the game.

entry_position.description: A narrow crack in the cliff face at the end of the cliffside path. Easy to miss on first visit.

discovery_triggers.description: Villager at the well mentions seeing a strange light on the cliffside at night
Rib-Addi mentions he used to go to 'the crack in the cliff' to think when he was young
Player simply walks to the end of the path and notices the crack

options.description: Anyone can enter — no skill required. Just have to find it.

contents.description: A small dry cave looking out over the sea through a crack in the rock. The view faces west. At sunset the light is extraordinary.
Scratched into the wall — rough drawings of a ship, stars, and an arrow pointing west. Clearly very old. Clearly made by someone sitting here, thinking.
A small tin box wedged into a rock crack. Rusted shut.

loot.description: A coin from a foreign city. Someone kept it here for a long time. The initials scratched on the back match your father's name.
A torn piece of a hand-drawn map showing the coastline near Kefr-Yamm and two small coves not marked on any official harbor map.

reward_summary.emotional_payoff: First hint that the player's father was also drawn to the west. Seeds the backstory without explaining it.
reward_summary.map_reward: Reveals two hidden coves near Kefr-Yamm usable for smuggling or hiding cargo

quests.purpose: Teaches sailing, docking, NPC interaction, and selling in a new city

steps.hint: Ask anyone in Sidon's dock district

steps.description: Optional: sell any goods you brought from Kefr-Yamm while in Sidon
Learn that a shipment of rope he ordered from Tyre never arrived
Ask at the Grand Bazaar about a shipment of rope sent to Kefr-Yamm
Shipment was intercepted by a merchant who claimed non-payment

options.description: Pay the merchant 60 silver to release the shipment
Find Dagon's original payment receipt hidden in Tyre's harbor records
Use reputation (requires reputation_tyre 20+) to pressure the merchant

steps.description: Rib-Addi asks you to find a specific type of shell — only found near Kition, Cyprus. He held one once, decades ago, and has wanted it back ever since.
Found on the beach at low tide near Kition. Not sold in any shop.

reward.note: No silver reward. Pure lore and character payoff. The navigation secret Rib-Addi reveals is mechanically valuable for the final voyage.

economy.note: Kefr-Yamm has no fees or bureaucracy. It is the only location in the game where the player can trade completely freely. This contrast is intentional — it makes Tyre's fees feel like a real step up in complexity.
